provenance.mapping_decision: Problem 122 is not a retroactive replacement for frozen candidate 105 or candidate 101. Candidate 105 performs inverse identification from supplied fermionic-Gaussian observations, while candidate 101 optimizes a six-angle probe using mixed-state QFIM. Problem 122 instead synthesizes a sparse integer portfolio of implementable binary experiments, projects classical Fisher information through readout and coherent nuisance directions, and must generalize from public axis anchors to hidden coupled points.

title: Robust nuisance-projected fermionic-Gaussian experiment portfolio
difficulty_explanation: A solver must obtain normalized five-parameter likelihood derivatives from TensorCircuit FGSSimulator, form the nuisance-projected classical Fisher matrix rather than QFIM or the full Fisher determinant, and synthesize a sparse, granular, two-budget integer allocation that improves both D- and E-optimality on coupled hidden points. The prompt specifies correctness but does not disclose the reference allocation or its greedy repair strategy.
solution_explanation: The compact expert uses TensorCircuit for every fermionic-Gaussian probability, central differences for four nonlinear coordinates, the exact readout-contrast derivative, a public-plus-Hadamard robust design set, and a deterministic block-granular greedy portfolio constructor with feasibility lookahead.
verification_explanation: The scoring oracle never imports or calls TensorCircuit. It independently evolves a complex128 Bogoliubov isometry, recomputes all probabilities, derivatives, Fisher matrices, Schur complements, certificates, hidden metrics, and budgets, checks its covariance convention against a direct tiny Fock-space Jordan-Wigner evolution, compares three- and five-point derivatives, and rejects scientific and schema mutants. The optional local self-test separately loads the expert through real TensorCircuit when installed or an explicitly non-evidentiary semantic shim when absent.

claim_boundary: This is a reduced deterministic design-only prototype for a synthetic fermionic-Gaussian experiment-design diagnostic. It does not estimate laboratory Fisher information, certify asymptotic attainability, model finite-shot estimator bias, or establish optimality of the expert allocation. The local public development key is not secret. The evaluator's local semantic FGS shim, when used because TensorCircuit is unavailable, checks expert API intent only and is not TensorCircuit execution evidence. No Docker, pinned TensorCircuit image, Harbor, private prequalification, solver model, or hardness trial has run, and no model-hardness claim is made.
